problem.question: A company has 200 employees.  60% of the employees drive to work.  Of the employees who don't drive to work, half take public transportation. How many more employees drive to work than take public transportation?
problem.answer:
Drive to work:200(.60)=<<200*.60=120>>120
Don't Drive to work:200-120=<<200-120=80>>80
Public Transportation:80(.50)=40 employees
80-40=<<80-40=40>>40 employees
#### 40

generation.text:
The number of employees who drive to work is 200(.60)=120
The number of employees who don't drive to work is 200-120=80
Of the employees who don't drive to work, 80/2=40 take public transportation
There are 120-40=80 employees who drive to work and take public transportation
The final answer is \boxed{80}.
